questions.text:
Read the passage provided (Text A — a personal essay about working on a fishing boat during a gap year).

Discuss how the writer explores the ways unfamiliar experiences shape a person's sense of self, referring to at least TWO specific aspects of written texts.
questions.markingGuide:
ACHIEVED (3-4 marks): Develop a relevant critical discussion in response to the question, showing engagement with the text. Make and evaluate a range of relevant points showing understanding of how at least TWO aspects of the text have been crafted to create meaning. Include specific and relevant details from the text to support the discussion.

MERIT (5-6 marks): Develop a convincing critical discussion showing informed engagement with the text. Make and evaluate relevant points showing convincing understanding of how at least TWO aspects have been crafted to create meaning. Begin to weave specific details from the text into the response to effectively support the discussion. Potentially link points to matters beyond the text.

EXCELLENCE (7-8 marks): Develop a sophisticated or original critical discussion showing insightful engagement with the text. Make and evaluate relevant points showing perceptive understanding of how at least TWO aspects have been crafted to create meaning. Weave specific and judiciously chosen details into the response to effectively support and expand the discussion. Trace the development of ideas throughout the text and link points to other contexts such as human experience, society, and the wider world.

Relevant aspects might include: audiences and purposes; ideas (e.g. discomfort as a catalyst for growth, the gap between expectation and reality, physical labour as a form of self-knowledge, camaraderie forged through shared hardship); language features (e.g. visceral sensory detail — salt, cold, exhaustion; contrast between the narrator's earlier naivety and later understanding; colloquial language creating authenticity; metaphor connecting the sea to emotional states); structures (e.g. chronological progression tracking personal change, short paragraphs during intense moments, reflective passages that step back from the action).

questions.text:
Read the poem provided (Text B — a poem about a house being demolished in a neighbourhood undergoing development).

Discuss how the writer explores ideas about loss and progress, referring to at least TWO specific aspects of written texts.

Relevant aspects might include: audiences and purposes; ideas (e.g. what is lost when old buildings are replaced, the tension between preservation and modernisation, the house as a vessel for collective memory, who benefits from development); language features (e.g. personification of the house, violent or mechanical imagery of demolition, contrast between domestic warmth and industrial coldness, elegiac tone); structures (e.g. the poem moves from the standing house to its destruction, stanza breaks marking stages of loss, a shift in the final stanza from grief to resignation or defiance).

questions.text:
Refer to BOTH Text A and Text B.

Discuss how the writers explore the ways people respond to change that is beyond their control, referring to at least TWO specific aspects of written texts. You may refer to one or both texts in your response.
questions.markingGuide:
ACHIEVED (3-4 marks): Develop a relevant critical discussion in response to the question, showing engagement with the text(s). Make and evaluate a range of relevant points showing understanding of how at least TWO aspects of the text(s) have been crafted to create meaning. Include specific and relevant details from the text(s) to support the discussion.

MERIT (5-6 marks): Develop a convincing critical discussion showing informed engagement with the text(s). Make and evaluate relevant points showing convincing understanding of how at least TWO aspects have been crafted to create meaning. Begin to weave specific details from the text(s) into the response to effectively support the discussion. Potentially link points to matters beyond the text(s).

EXCELLENCE (7-8 marks): Develop a sophisticated or original critical discussion showing insightful engagement with the text(s). Make and evaluate relevant points showing perceptive understanding of how at least TWO aspects have been crafted to create meaning. Weave specific and judiciously chosen details into the response to effectively support and expand the discussion. Trace the development of ideas throughout the text(s) and link points to other contexts such as human experience, society, and the wider world.

Relevant aspects might include: audiences and purposes; ideas (e.g. both texts involve individuals navigating change imposed by external forces — the sea in Text A, urban development in Text B; one change leads to personal growth while the other involves communal grief; adaptation versus resistance; what we gain and lose when the world around us shifts); language features (e.g. both use sensory language but to different emotional ends — exhilaration versus mourning; personal pronouns position the reader differently in each text; tone shifts from uncertainty to acceptance in the prose, from tenderness to anger in the poem); structures (e.g. the prose tracks a linear transformation while the poem compresses time; both use specific physical details to anchor abstract ideas about change).
